claims.text: The initial CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy is single-phase FCC.
The initial alloy is produced by powder metallurgy.
Adding 1–2 vol% surface-functionalized graphene nanoplatelets will improve effective heat-transfer capability by 30–40%.
The graphene addition will limit the reduction in yield strength to less than 5% under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
Surface functionalization enhances compatibility and bonding between graphene nanoplatelets and the metal matrix.
High-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering can produce a uniform dispersion of graphene nanoplatelets in the alloy.
The functionalized graphene nanoplatelets will bridge grain boundaries without forming deleterious secondary phases.
Uniformly dispersed graphene nanoplatelets will create enhanced thermal-conduction paths.
Strongly bonded graphene nanoplatelets will permit sufficient load transfer across the microstructure.
Graphene nanoplatelets have in-plane thermal conductivity exceeding 2000 W/m·K.
Uniformly distributed graphene nanoplatelets form an interconnected network in the HEA.
The interconnected graphene network facilitates phonon and electron heat transfer across the alloy.
Functionalization produces strong interfacial bonding that promotes efficient load transfer.
Strong interfacial bonding inhibits crack initiation despite thermal-expansion mismatch.
The modified HEA will retain its heat-transfer and mechanical benefits during cyclic thermal exposure from 600 to 800 °C.
Failure to achieve uniform nanoplatelet dispersion or sufficient interfacial bonding may alter the expected outcome.
